answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require stake-linked identity deposits: each agent locks a deposit, its jade, a scarce credential token that is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. New identities start with a trust delta of zero reputation and throttled transaction limits, so an attacker must pay the deposit and build history for every fake. Peers mirror each other's identity graphs, cross-checking behavioral fingerprints, so a swarm of clones shows up as an unnatural cluster and gets quarantined before it can transact.
